t: #3427 Sum of Variable Length Subarrays — Prefix Sums
o: For every index i we must sum the contiguous block of nums ending at i and starting at max(0, i - nums[i]), then add all those block sums together. In example 1, i=0 gives [2]=2, i=1 gives [2,3]=5, i=2 gives [3,1]=4, totaling 11. With n ≤ 100 even an O(n²) sweep is instant, but the natural follow-up asks for large n, where a prefix-sum array answers each block sum in O(1).
k: Each query is a range sum nums[start..i], perfect for prefix sums.
start = max(0, i - nums[i]) clamps to the array's left edge.

a.i: Directly simulate the definition: for each i, loop from start to i adding elements. With n ≤ 100 this is at most 10,000 additions.
s: For each i compute start = max(0, i - nums[i]).
Inner loop accumulates nums[start..i] into the answer.
a.t: O(n²) — for each of n indices we scan up to n elements

a.i: Build pre where pre[i+1] = nums[0..i] summed. Then each block sum is pre[i+1] - pre[start], giving linear time — the scalable solution interviewers look for.
s: Build the prefix array in one pass.
Answer each i as pre[i+1] - pre[max(0, i - nums[i])].
a.t: O(n) — one pass to build prefixes, one to answer

w: Use the prefix-sum version in an interview; mention brute force only as a warm-up. Pitfalls: forgetting the max(0, ...) clamp at the left edge and integer overflow for large n (use 64-bit). Follow-ups: what if starts were given by a separate array, or queries were online?
